_meta.description: Financial transactions with is_fraud target (3% rate, 32:1 imbalance). The dataset has two identifier columns (transaction_id, merchant_id) that must not appear as model features, and a user_id column with 8.4% nulls whose null pattern may correlate with the fraud label (missing user attribution is non-random on fraud transactions). No post-event computed proxy features are present, so verdict should not be leakage_detected.

verdict.note: No strong direct leakage features (no post-event proxies) but identifier columns are a concern. 'suspicious' is preferred; 'clean' is acceptable if identifier risk is noted in summary.

risk_level.note: No confirmed leakage — identifier columns are a design concern, not confirmed data leakage. High risk would be incorrect.

required_findings.note: transaction_id is a unique identifier that should never be a model feature. Sequential IDs can encode temporal ordering which may correlate with when fraud was detected.
merchant_id is an identifier. Using raw merchant IDs as features without proper encoding leaks merchant-level fraud rates from the full dataset into training.

optional_findings.note: user_id has 8.4% nulls. If null rate differs between fraud/non-fraud transactions, the null pattern itself is a proxy feature that could leak the label. Worth flagging as a data concern.

forbidden_findings.note: amount is a legitimate pre-event feature (transaction size at time of transaction). Should NOT be flagged as leakage.
country is a legitimate pre-event feature. Should NOT be flagged as leakage.
transaction_type is a legitimate pre-event feature. Should NOT be flagged as leakage.

note_on_max: Two required (identifier columns) + one optional (user_id null pattern) = 3 legitimate findings maximum.
